title: Half a Plate of Colour: Small Truths About Eating Well
title_zh: 半盘色彩：关于吃得好的几个小真相
intro_zh: 本文约 519 词，围绕“健康饮食的小常识”展开，从食物颜色、餐盘比例、膳食纤维、含糖饮料、进食速度到隐形盐，给出具体数据与可操作建议，含 6 个 CET-4 核心词，适合四级阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: Stand in any supermarket and you will see shelves full of promises: low-fat biscuits, sugar-free sweets, vitamin water. Yet the plainest advice from doctors is also the hardest to follow — eat more plants, less salt, and stop before you feel full. The good news is that a few sensible rules can make a real difference, and they cost almost nothing.
paragraphs.zh: 站在任何一家超市里，你都会看到货架上满是承诺：低脂饼干、无糖糖果、维生素水。然而医生给出的最朴素的建议，往往也最难做到——多吃植物性食物，少吃盐，在感到饱之前就停下。好消息是，几条明智的小规则就能带来实实在在的改变，而且几乎不花什么钱。

paragraphs.en: The first rule is colour. The World Health Organization suggests that adults eat at least 400 grams of fruit and vegetables a day — about five small portions. Each colour carries its own nutrients: orange carrots provide vitamin A, red tomatoes provide lycopene, and dark green leaves provide iron and calcium. A plate with three colours is usually a plate with three kinds of protection.
paragraphs.zh: 第一条规则是颜色。世界卫生组织建议成年人每天至少吃 400 克水果和蔬菜——大约五小份。每种颜色都带着自己的营养素：橙色的胡萝卜提供维生素 A，红色的番茄提供番茄红素，深绿色的叶子菜提供铁和钙。一盘有三种颜色的食物，通常就是三种保护。

paragraphs.en: Nutritionists often draw a plate instead of writing a list. Imagine yours cut into four parts: two filled with vegetables or salad, one with rice, bread or noodles, and one with fish, eggs, beans or meat. Nothing is banned; the shape of the meal does the work. People who arrange food this way tend to eat more vegetables without ever feeling that they are on a diet.
paragraphs.zh: 营养学家常常画一只餐盘，而不是列一张清单。设想把你的盘子分成四份：两份装满蔬菜或沙拉，一份装米饭、面包或面条，一份装鱼、蛋、豆类或肉。没有什么是被禁止的；是这一餐的形状在起作用。这样摆放食物的人往往吃到更多蔬菜，却从不觉得自己在节食。

paragraphs.en: The second rule is fiber. Adults need about 25 to 30 grams a day, yet most of us get barely half that. Fiber slows the release of sugar into the blood and keeps you full for longer. An apple offers about 4 grams; a bowl of beans, about 15. Whole grains, nuts and vegetables are the cheapest sources, and they satisfy hunger far better than a bag of crisps.
paragraphs.zh: 第二条规则是膳食纤维。成年人每天需要大约 25 到 30 克，而我们大多数人连一半都吃不到。纤维能减缓糖分进入血液的速度，并让你更长时间不饿。一个苹果约含 4 克，一碗豆子约含 15 克。全谷物、坚果和蔬菜是最便宜的来源，而且它们解除饥饿的效果远胜一袋薯片。

paragraphs.en: Then read the back of the packet, not the front. A 500-millilitre bottle of fruit juice may hold 50 grams of sugar — ten teaspoons — even though the picture on it shows a sunny orchard. WHO advises keeping free sugars below 10 percent of daily energy, and says 5 percent brings extra benefit. Checking the sugar line on a label takes five seconds and can save you a hundred grams a day.
paragraphs.zh: 然后请看包装的背面，而不是正面。一瓶 500 毫升的果汁可能含 50 克糖——十茶匙——尽管瓶身上的图片画着一片阳光下的果园。世界卫生组织建议把游离糖控制在每日能量的 10% 以下，并表示降到 5% 会带来额外好处。看一眼标签上的糖那一行只花五秒，却能让你每天少摄入上百克糖。

paragraphs.en: Slow down. Your brain needs about twenty minutes to receive the signal that food has arrived. People who finish a meal in eight minutes often reach for a second helping before that message lands. Putting the fork down between bites, or drinking a glass of water first, gives the body time to catch up. Studies of large groups repeatedly link fast eating with higher body weight.
paragraphs.zh: 慢一点。你的大脑大约需要二十分钟才能接收到“食物到了”的信号。八分钟吃完一餐的人，往往在那条信息到达之前就又添了一份。每吃几口就把叉子放下，或者先喝一杯水，能留给身体追赶的时间。对大规模人群的研究一再把吃得太快与更高的体重联系起来。

paragraphs.en: Salt hides where you least expect it: in bread, instant noodles, soy sauce and processed meat. WHO suggests less than 5 grams of salt a day — roughly one level teaspoon — yet many of us eat twice that. Water is the simplest drink, while sweet tea and cola add sugar with no nutrients at all. A useful swap: sparkling water with lemon instead of a fizzy drink, or a handful of nuts instead of biscuits at four o'clock.
paragraphs.zh: 盐藏在你最想不到的地方：面包、方便面、酱油和加工肉制品里。世界卫生组织建议每天吃盐少于 5 克——大约一平茶匙——可我们许多人吃的是这个量的两倍。水是最简单的饮品，而甜茶和可乐只增加糖，毫无营养。一个有用的替换办法：用加柠檬的气泡水代替碳酸饮料，或者在下午四点用一把坚果代替饼干。

paragraphs.en: No single food decides your health, and no single meal ruins it. What matters is the pattern you repeat over weeks: a little more colour, a little more fiber, a little less salt and sugar. Start with one change you can keep — a piece of fruit at breakfast, perhaps — and let the rest follow.
paragraphs.zh: 没有哪一种食物能决定你的健康，也没有哪一顿饭会把它毁掉。真正重要的是你几周以来重复的那个模式：多一点颜色，多一点纤维，少一点盐和糖。从一项你能坚持的改变开始——比如早餐加一个水果——其余的会随之而来。

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To explain why supermarkets sell unhealthy products.
To warn readers that fruit and vegetables can be harmful.
To offer practical, science-based tips for eating better.
To compare home cooking with restaurant meals.
questions.explain: 全文围绕健康饮食的几条小常识展开：颜色多样、餐盘比例、纤维、看标签、放慢速度、隐形盐和替换饮品，属于“提供实用且基于科学的饮食建议”，故选第三项。第一项只是开头场景，第二项与原文相反，第四项文中未作比较。

questions.q: According to the passage, how much fiber do adults need each day?
questions.explain: 第四段明确写道 Adults need about 25 to 30 grams a day。4 克是一个苹果的纤维含量，15 克是一碗豆子的含量，50 克是果汁里可能含的糖量，均为干扰项。

questions.q: Why does the author mention that the brain needs about twenty minutes to get the message that food has arrived?
options: To show that preparing a meal takes a long time.
To explain why people who eat fast tend to eat more.
To prove that water is better than juice.
To argue that lunch should last at least an hour.
questions.explain: 第六段说明大脑接收饱腹信号需要约二十分钟，吃得太快的人在信号到达前就已添了第二份，因此该细节是为了解释吃饭快的人为何吃得更多，选第二项。文中并未主张午餐要吃一小时。

questions.q: The word 'swap' in the seventh paragraph is closest in meaning to ____.
questions.explain: 该句举例说明用加柠檬的气泡水代替碳酸饮料、用坚果代替饼干，因此 swap 意为“替换、交换”，与 exchange 最接近。addition（增加）、recipe（食谱）、warning（警告）均不符合语境。
